nodes.title: Our minGain gate cannot resolve anything below 3 points, and its own history says so
nodes.body:
The gate as written is `score - taskBest >= minGain - 1e-9` with minGain defaulting to 0.05 on a 0-1 scale, so it treats a 5-point improvement as detectable. Wave-2 measured the arithmetic: run-level SD of agentic pass@1 across ten runs on 500 SWE-bench-Verified tasks is sigma 0.7-1.8 pp, so n >= 2((1.96+0.84)/(Delta/sigma))^2 per arm, which is 8-36 runs to detect 1 pp and 8-13 to detect 2 pp. Our own earlier observation is worse than that: ten reruns of one configuration spread 2.2-6.0 points.

Combining them, a single draw differing by 5 points from the historical best cannot distinguish a real improvement from a lucky run, and a 1-point difference is pure noise. The gate is therefore not a filter, it is a coin that lands head often enough to look like one. This is exactly PACE's finding that greedy acceptance under stochasticity is self-p-hacking, with a 72-100% false-commit rate — we simply have the pathological acceptor without its name.

The mechanism-level fix is not to raise minGain, which only trades false accepts for false rejects without knowing either rate. It is to make the comparison paired within a task (same eval items, before and after) so item difficulty cancels, and to require the delta to exceed a stated multiple of the measured sigma for that task, refusing to decide when it does not. That costs runs we currently do not spend, which is the honest price.

Limitation: my sigma comes from other people's benchmarks, not from our ledger. Our ledger has 441 attempts but almost no repeated-measurement structure — the same task on the same tree twice is rare — so we cannot yet estimate our own sigma, which is itself the first thing to fix.

nodes.title: Five of thirty-five campaign specs are red and the guard cannot see any of them
nodes.body:
Ran all 35 specs under tests/self*/: 30 green, 5 red, 146 assertions total. scripts/test-all.mjs excludes tests/self*/ by design (they are the specs a campaign is still satisfying) and reports 157/157 green. The five failures are tests/self2/plateau.test.mjs 14/15, and four spec files that throw an AssertionError: tests/self5/holdout-gate.test.mjs, tests/self5/no-test-edits.test.mjs, tests/self8/human-node.test.mjs, tests/self9/holdout-report.test.mjs.

The exclusion is right while a campaign runs and becomes a blind spot when it stops. plateau.js, deferred.js, exposure.js and sampling.js are all wired into round.js and are covered only by excluded specs, so a later promotion that breaks them keeps the guard green. test-all.mjs already supports the fix it needs through its `standing` array: a finished campaign's spec should be moved there.

Two of the five failures are themselves informative rather than stale. In holdout-gate the round ends no-gain where the spec requires holdout-failed, because rejectedByHoldout is defined as basePass && checks.holdout === false, so when the base tree already passes the verifier the holdout rejection is dropped; quality.js then counts zero holdout failure for a campaign whose holdout did fire. In no-test-edits a source-only change fails to promote, which is the same earned-gate branch seen from the other side.
